passages: A sailing ship traditionally has at least one mast to hold up sails. These sails use the wind to move the ship. The rigging helps support the sails on the mast, all of which are attached to the superstructure of the ship; the hull. Sailing across oceans can be dangerous due to a lack of wind, which leads to being becalmed, or too much wind which may direct the ship in an undesirable direction. With the emergence of steamships in the early 19th century, a vessel containing a steam engine allowed greater manoeuvrability from ships. Inevitably, steamships replaced all sailing ships. By 2006, automated sails were developed, as such advancement in hybrid ships progressed it lead the way for reinvigorating the age of sail.

Gaming has grown considerably over the past decade. Games are now ubiquitous, easily accessible and readily available. Counterintuitively, the rise of the video game industry has arguably strengthened the appeal of board games. Due to the prevalence of video games, more people than ever are familiar with the concept of playing games. Online video games typically allow for player cooperation via the internet. One factor for the growth in board games is that they provide direct interaction with people, something video games appear to be moving away from. Spearheading the rise of board games are Eurogames – games that emphasise economic themes, reduce chance, and are designed to keep all players involved until it ends.

Conventional wisdom is a generally accepted range of explanations or ideas that the public believe as true. Normally, conventional wisdom is therefore used as an axiom by which to determine the context or validity of other truth claims. This is arguably regarded as a challenge in incorporating and interpreting new information. Once conventional wisdom sets in, convenient ideas become assumptions. As such, new ideas which contradict or irritate these conventions are often met with great ideological obstacles.

One popular piece of conventional wisdom is that salt in your diet is bad for you. The origins of this claim come from organisations like the American Heart Association. However, scientific data suggests that there is no correlation between salt intake, and for example, heart disease.

The boiling frog is an anecdote used as a metaphor that describes a frog being put into boiling water. According to the story, if a frog were to be placed into water already boiling, it would jump out. However, if the frog were to be placed into cold water that was eventually brought to boil, it would not notice the danger and be cooked to death. This story is analogous to a reluctance in noticing potential threats if they gradually appear.

Debate surrounds the appropriate use of the boiling frog story due to its inaccuracy regarding the real behaviour of frogs. Some commentators point out that while the story may be useful for metaphor, it is necessary to point out that, in reality, this does not occur. Others have likened the boiling frog to the metaphor about an ostrich with its head in the sand.

Confirmation bias is a systematic error in inductive reasoning whereby one interprets, remembers and comprehends information in a way that confirms their pre-existing beliefs or explanations. Typically, someone displaying confirmation bias is selective with information, most notably with emotionally relevant topics. Confirmation bias can therefore lead us to build strongly held views that could lead to some unbalanced perspectives.

Some commentators suggest that confirmation bias is unintentional rather than a decisive action, aimed at allowing us to make sense of new information heuristically. It is proposed that consistently building alternate hypotheses in parallel is demanding on the mind and does not readily allow one to make sense of complex information.

Drinking water from plastic bottles has become ubiquitous in many parts of the world. It is believed to be healthier than tap water, the main argument being that tap water typically contains more metal contaminants as a result of the piping. It is also claimed to be safer. In communities that have problematic water piping, bottled water consumption is notably higher. However, some studies suggest that bottled water is no healthier than tap water, with claims that bottled water is less healthy. One great concern from bottled water critics is the massive environmental impact of the disposable plastic bottles. With recycling rates remaining low, the number of plastic bottles produced to maintain the demand for bottled water has exacerbated the problem of overburdened landfills.

Glamping is a combination of the words ‘glamour’ and ‘camping.’ It describes the activity of camping with luxurious amenities. Typically, this is to fulfil a desire for escapism often ascribed with camping, but with the benefits of comfortable living. Glamping has seen a rise in popularity during the 21st century, especially from 2005 onwards when the word ‘glamping’ came into fashion. The emergence of this popularity is in large part due to its affordability. Today, luxury camping is not exclusively available to the rich. Many accommodations that promote glamping aim to be affordable for most price ranges. Although glamping may promote comfort over the minimalism of camping, the focus remains on outdoor recreation.

Food colouring is any substance added to food or drink that gives it a colour. Typically, the food is transformed to a colour that is not naturally occurring. Given that the colour of food changes how one perceives it, food colourings are used to influence how consumers judge the flavour of the item. Colouring can sometimes be for beneficial purposes such as lengthening its shelf life. Other reasons could simply be to make the food more attractive. Furthermore, food colouring is also used in many other inedible products, generally for aesthetic purposes.

A popular assumption surrounding food colouring is that it has negative health effects, namely hyperactivity in children. However, as of 2017, there is no evidence to support these claims. There are a few circumstances where there is a possible correlation between colouring and perceived hyperactivity, though the link is tenuous and limited.

In order to deactivate the alarm, you need to follow these instructions:

• Locate the main alarm panel
• Unlock the door with the password “C1278X”
• Press the button marked “deactivate” on the main alarm panel
• Locate the system battery in the main alarm panel*
• Remove the battery by pressing the button “detach”

*If you are unable to locate system battery:

• Locate the main circuit board
• Unlock the panel with the password “0X841”
• Detach the red wires marked “AC” and “Power”
• DO NOT remove any black wires
• DO NOT allow the wires to come into contact with other wires

If there are any further problems, please do not hesitate to contact the online help service.

After purchasing your book online, follow these instructions to assemble it yourself:

• Print out your purchased PDF file.
• Locate the cover page and cut it in half, following the indicated line.
• One by one, or in groups of maximum five, fold each page or pages in half, making sure the numbers are in chronological order.
• Each print out page will therefore create four book pages.
• Place the two pieces of the cut cover page on the front and bottom of the interior pages.
• Staple the left-hand side of the book.

Your newly purchased book is now ready to be read!

The following instructions will help you to use the printer/scanner efficiently:

To Copy:

• Place the side of the document you want to copy face-down.
• Ensure the copier lid is down.
• Press the black button followed by the Start button for a black and white copy.

To Scan:

• Place the document you wish to scan face-down, as you would if you were making a photocopy.
• Use the arrow console to navigate to the ‘Scan’ option.
• Press the black button to confirm your selection choices.

Cleaning printheads:

• Use the arrow console to highlight ‘Maintenance.’ Press the black button to confirm.
• Navigate to and select ‘Colour management.’
• Follow the on-screen instructions.

N.B. If you are still seeing streaks in your print outs, consider replacing the printheads. See section 3.4 for more information.

The following instructions provide a useful guide in setting up a musical performance in small spaces:

• Place 2 microphones in the centre of the stage
• Place 1 speaker at the front, facing towards the performer, for them to hear themselves
• Place 2 speakers at the sides, facing towards the audience, for them to hear the music
• Plug cables into all speakers, instruments and microphones
• Keep the cables along the stage edge where they are safe - away from the performer to avoid potential hazards
• Plug cables into the mixing desk, be sure to note the numbers – for example, microphone = 1
• Set volume levels, high or low, to what is appropriate for the performance space

This set-up will aptly prepare you for many potential situations as it covers various musical styles that require this layout.

N.B. *Mixing desk = controls the volume levels of all inputs
